rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.list_sources.mcp.description` consists only of the quoted text `List available project file nodes.` That is the description the list_sources MCP tool advertises. The text names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or delegation through a named interface.

An implementation could build the definition by another route, such as a constant, a different JSON builder, or a different function. It would still advertise the same description, so every clause concerns observable output only. The structure is discretionary, and no structural obligation needs implementation evidence.

The supplied root `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#impl[Session<'_,%20D>/ToolSession<D>]/fn[definitions]` does emit the exact description for the `LIST_SOURCES` tool. It carries the `{impl}` marker for this requirement. That is consistent with the text, but it is not needed to satisfy a structural obligation.

behavioral: The requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.list_sources.mcp.description` has one observable obligation. The published `list_sources` tool description must be exactly `List available project file nodes.`

The test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[published_tool_descriptions_match_the_contract]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It builds a `ProjectSources` and reads the published tool definitions. It then finds the tool named `list_sources`. The `unwrap` fails the test if the tool is missing. Finally, `assert_eq!` compares the tool's `description` with the exact required string.

A wrong, altered or missing description would fail this test. I found no other conditions, boundaries or modes in the requirement text that need tests.
